title: Severe Anaphylaxis with NRB & Epinephrine
text: At 14:32, patient was conscious but experiencing difficulty breathing. Administered oxygen at 10 liters per minute through a non-rebreather mask. At 14:36, administered 0.3 milligrams of epinephrine intramuscularly. Patient's breathing improved at 14:40.
highlight: Standard multi-event ALS workflow with oxygen and epinephrine

title: Unresponsive Opioid Overdose
text: At 03:12, dispatched to unresponsive adult. Found cyanotic with shallow respirations. At 03:15, administered 2 mg of naloxone intranasally. At 03:18, patient regained spontaneous breathing and consciousness.

title: Acute Chest Pain with Prior Aspirin
text: At 19:45, arrived on scene for 58yo male experiencing substernal chest pressure. Patient had received aspirin before our arrival from family. We performed a 12-lead ECG at 19:48 showing ST elevation. Administered 0.4 mg nitroglycerin sublingually at 19:50.
highlight: Prior administration detection + 12-lead procedure + SL route

title: Severe Trauma with Withheld Morphine
text: At 11:20, patient presented with compound fracture of right tibia. We prepared morphine but did not administer it due to sudden drop in systolic blood pressure below 85. Applied extremity splinting at 11:25.

title: Angina with Patient Refusal
text: At 16:05, evaluated 62yo female with radiating arm pain. Offered nitroglycerin, but patient refused nitroglycerin due to severe headache history. Administered oxygen at 4 liters per minute via nasal cannula at 16:08.

title: Cardiac Arrest with On-Scene Dosage Correction
text: At 08:15, initiated CPR and bag-valve-mask ventilation. At 08:18, pushed 1 mg epinephrine IV. Correction: the dose was 0.03 mg, not 0.3 mg.
highlight: In-line errata linking and superseded event flagging

title: Unrecorded Medication Dose
text: At 13:00, patient agitated. Administered midazolam intravenously; exact dose was not recorded on scene. Patient settled at 13:08.
highlight: Missing dosage warning without fabricating a value

title: Missing Drug Name with Dose Recorded
text: At 21:10, administered 5 mg; medication name not recorded. Patient vitals stable.
highlight: Unknown medication entity flagged for urgent review

title: Diabetic Emergency with Dextrose
text: At 07:45, blood glucose measured at 34 mg/dL. Established peripheral IV access. Administered 25 grams of dextrose intravenously at 07:50. Patient alert and oriented at 07:58.
highlight: IV access procedure + Gram units + Dextrose

title: Severe Asthma with Duoneb Inhalation
text: At 15:20, severe wheezing and retraction noted. Administered albuterol 2.5 mg via nebulizer at 15:22. Continued oxygen at 6 L/min.

title: Explicit Contraindication Negation
text: At 22:30, severe abdominal pain. Do not administer morphine due to suspected biliary colic. Placed patient on monitor.

title: Spoken Numbers and Military Time
text: At 1436 hours, gave point three milligrams epinephrine intramuscularly. At 1440 hours, gave two hundred and fifty milliliters saline IV.
highlight: Spoken numbers ('point three', 'two hundred and fifty') + military time
